methodology: Manual review of programs/drift/src/controller/orders.rs on the protocol-v2 master branch. Searched for same-owner / self-trade / self-match rejection at the fill path.

evidence.interpretation: Drift handles the same-authority-on-both-sides case by skipping maker_stats lookup, not by rejecting the fill. Self-trades are structurally permitted.

findings.socialisationNote: Insurance Fund + ADL queue are core protocol features. Lost $270M+ in the April 2026 exploit via a related but different attack vector (durable nonce, not F7). Socialisation via ADL is documented.
findings.residualClaimSurface: TBD - need to trace whether a same-owner pair can claim their own socialised counterparty loss
findings.classification: RED (permits self-match, has insurance, residual-claim surface not yet disproven)
findings.confidence: high on self-match permission, medium on overall F7-class exposure pending residual-claim trace

notes: Drift has been under heavy scrutiny since April 2026. Any F7-class vulnerability would likely be detected quickly by the team.

The specific F7 attack requires: (1) self-match allowed, (2) insurance absorbs bankrupt side, (3) winning side can claim a residual that grew by the absorbed amount. Item 1 confirmed. Items 2 and 3 need further trace.
Recommended: private disclosure DM to Drift before any publication.
